newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: VILNIAUS BANK TO SEEK NEW RATINGS IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: VILNIAUS BANK TO SEEK NEW RATINGS IN 1997.

text.p: Lithuania's Vilniaus Bank said on Wednesday that it would seek new ratings in 1997, including a second rating from Thomson BankWatch.
"Vilniaus Bank has decided to order a new credit rating from Thomson plus a rating from a second agency," the chairman of the bank's board, Julius Niedvaras, told Reuters.
"We have sent proposals to agencies but have not entered negotiations yet," he said.
"We will formally request the rating in the middle of summer and expect the results in the autumn," he added.
He declined to name the other agencies approached by the bank.

Vilniaus Bank, the largest private bank in Lithuania, acquired an LC-1 short-term local currency debt rating from Thomson, its highest, last October. It was also given a BB- for long-term local currency debt.
Niedvaras said that the bank required additional ratings because it planned to seek subordinated and syndicated loans as well as new investments.
Rating agency IBCA said earlier on Wednesday that it was in talks with a number of Lithuanian banks and planned to grant ratings to banks in the country this year.
